title: Scott Cunningham — Causal Inference: The Remix, Potential Outcomes and Randomization
use: Method reference for potential outcomes, observed-outcome identity, ATE/ATT, selection decomposition, randomized assignment and treatment stability. Original numerical examples and explicit finite-lottery proof are supplied in the chapter.
verification: Retrieved the author-hosted open chapter and inspected sections 4.2–4.5, including equations 4.4–4.8 and the selection/randomization/SUTVA discussion. Inspection covers these stable methods, not every claim in the live edition or a frozen publication version. Chapter distinguishes finite-sample realized imbalance from expectation over randomized assignment.

title: Scott Cunningham — Causal Inference: The Remix, Unconfoundedness
use: Conditional exchangeability, target-specific averaging, positivity/common support and the distinction between adjustment and regression extrapolation.
verification: Retrieved the author-hosted open chapter and inspected section 5.3: conditional independence, common support, weighted ATE derivation (equations 5.7 and 5.10–5.17), weaker ATT conditions, plus the later functional-form discussion. The manuscript explicitly separates population positivity from empirical cell counts and labels extrapolation as an additional assumption. No source numerical examples or code reproduced.

title: Carlos Cinelli, Andrew Forney and Judea Pearl — A Crash Course in Good and Bad Control (original university-hosted methodological note, 14 August 2019)
use: Primary-author university note on causal control roles, pre-treatment collider bias, mediator adjustment and why timing alone is insufficient. The chapter's structural and enumerative examples are original.
verification: Retrieved UCLA's original author note and inspected models 1–3, 7 and 11–16 and their explanatory paragraphs. In particular, model 7 describes a pre-treatment collider; models 11–12 explain blocked mediated channels; models 14–16 show that post-treatment timing alone does not settle validity. The note links a later extended article, but that article is not claimed as inspected.
